page: Microsoft Azure EC4ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the AMD EPYC 9V74 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs spread across 2 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, it features a 32 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The instance includes 32 GB of system memory, providing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside a bundled 161 GB local SSD for temporary storage. Hyper-V serves as the virtualization layer, and the CPU exposes vector and cryptographic instruction sets including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread capability counterbalanced by modest overall throughput. In synthetic tests, the instance achieves a top-quartile stress-ng single-core score of 3022.55, while its multi-core stress-ng score of 6010.36 sits in the bottom quartile due to the 4-vCPU ceiling. Geekbench testing reflects a similar profile, producing an average single-core score of 1873.0 alongside a lower-tier multi-core result of 4151.0 and software compilation score of 4988.0. Memory subsystem testing yields an average PassMark memory score of 2329.47, whereas transactional metrics such as Redis SET operations (5.3 million operations per second) and PassMark database operations (1925.59) track lower in cross-instance comparisons.

The 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio paired with fast single-core response makes this instance efficient for memory-intensive services that do not demand extensive core parallelism. Built-in local solid-state storage supports scratch data, temporary tables, and ephemeral caching without requiring external disk attachments for temporary I/O. The primary tradeoff lies in raw multi-threaded capacity, limiting performance on parallel build pipelines, compute-bound analytics, or heavy database concurrency. Suitable workloads include mid-sized in-memory caches, development databases, memory-bound microservices, and enterprise applications requiring high RAM per thread.

Operating on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance offers an 8 GB per vCPU allocation and supports modern instruction sets including AVX-512 and VAES. Benchmark evaluations show robust single-core compute, placing in the top quartile of stress-ng single-thread tests with a score of 3022.55, while overall multi-threaded throughput and database operations score lower due to the 4-thread envelope.
